triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the household-benefit bar previously fired on `household_has_member_disqualified_under_this_subsection and household_would_receive_increased_benefits_as_result_of_member_disqualification`, which never applied the statute's 'During the period of such ineligibility' limitation, and the permanent-disqualification branch tested opaque 'third occasion' booleans rather than an occasion count, so a fourth or later determination would not have triggered it.
triage.triage_notes: Mostly a rename and representation change, which is why I did not call it fidelity: first/second/two_year/permanent rule names were renamed, occasion booleans (`first_occasion_of_any_such_determination`, `second_...`, `third_...`) were replaced with an occasion-number input compared against new Count parameters, and the intentional-violation test was refactored to factor out `found_by_state_or_federal_court_or_administrative_agency`. The only arguable meaning changes are the two in pre_fix_wrong_because plus the == vs >= treatment of repeat controlled-substance and firearms findings. A regression to note: the pre-fix output `nonpermanent_ineligibility_period_years` (which returned 1 or 2) was deleted, and the 1-year/2-year period parameters it consumed are now declared but unused, so the module no longer emits a disqualification length. The summary excerpt also changed from '(b)(1) Any person...' to '(1) Any person...', an excerpt-only provenance change. Effective dates unchanged at 2008-10-01. Keep for reviewer pruning.
triage.verifier_justification: The first reader's anchor does not survive: the last-sentence household bar was already a rule before the change (source "7 U.S.C. 2015(b)(1), last sentence"), and the fix does not add the "During the period of such ineligibility" limitation as computable content — it renames two opaque undefined inputs into one (`household_has_member_disqualified_under_this_subsection_during_period_of_ineligibility`) and *drops* the "would receive increased benefits" conjunct, so nothing is added that the source states was missing. The one meaning change that does disagree with the source is the occasion tiering: pre-fix the permanent branch tested the exact-occasion boolean `third_occasion_of_any_such_determination`, so a person on a fourth determination (first/second/third all false) got `permanent_ineligibility_applies` false and `person_becomes_ineligible_for_further_snap_participation` false — fully eligible — while 7 U.S.C. 2015(b)(1)(iii)(I) plus (b)(3) ("Such periods of ineligibility ... shall remain in effect") make them permanently ineligible. The fix replaces that with an inclusive at-least bound on a count (`>= third_determination_occasion_number`, and likewise `>= controlled_substance_second_finding_occasion_number`) while deliberately keeping exact `==` for the one- and two-year tiers, which is a bound-strictness correction, not a missing clause.
triage.verifier_notes: Refutation of the original kind: the quoted statutory sentence ("During the period of such ineligibility, no household shall receive increased benefits...") is unchanged in the module summary across the diff, and the post-fix formula for that rule is a single opaque input whose name merely recites the clause. Per the rubric's provenance carve-out, a rename that puts statutory words into a variable name is not evidence the clause is now represented; and the diff removes a conjunct rather than adding coverage, which is the opposite shape from unrepresented_clause. Alternative kind worth considering: polarity_or_logic, since pre-fix a fourth determination made every branch false (fail-open to fully eligible); I preferred boundary_direction because the fix's decisive edit is the `==` vs `>=` split across tiers (== for 1st/2nd determination and 1st controlled-substance finding, >= for 3rd+ determination, 2nd+ controlled substance, 1st+ firearms). Caveats for pruning: the commit is a wholesale regeneration ("Regenerate validated US RuleSpec encodings", empty body) and PR #25 is titled "Encode 26 USC 63(c) standard deduction" with no mention of SNAP disqualification, so all evidence is internal to the diff; every numeric parameter (1, 2, 500) and every effective_from ('2008-10-01') is unchanged; and the diff also deletes the derived output `nonpermanent_ineligibility_period_years` (the 1/2/0-year selector), a coverage loss that is not a fidelity correction. Both pre and post are built entirely from undefined opaque inputs, so the fourth-occasion failure depends on reading `third_occasion_of_any_such_determination` literally — that reading is what the new occasion-count inputs and the rewritten test fixtures assume, but it is why I hold confidence at 0.55 rather than higher.
